# Choose your next small step

Use the learning paths and lesson exercises to build practical AI knowledge at your own pace.

Source: https://lj-web-management.github.io/guides.ai-skills.work/help/follow-a-learning-path/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Publisher: ai-skills.work

## Start with your immediate goal

Choose foundations if the concepts feel unfamiliar, practical skills if you have a task in mind, or career guidance if you are deciding what to learn next. The homepage highlights a short beginner route. These paths are suggestions, not entry requirements or qualifications.

- Read the summary before opening a longer guide.
- Skip familiar material and return when you need it.

## Practice before moving on

Each guide includes a worked example and a small exercise. Use public or invented information and check the result yourself. If an exercise feels difficult, return to the relevant section or try a simpler example. Understanding one task well is more useful than rushing through several pages.

- Write down one thing you learned.
- Keep a note of a question that still needs an answer.

## Check understanding and revisit gaps

Quizzes provide feedback on selected concepts. They are learning tools, not certifications or employment assessments. Review the explanations, return to the linked lessons, and try a new example. Your browser bookmarks can help you keep track of pages you want to revisit.

- Retake a quiz after reviewing its explanations.
- Use real-world practice to complement quiz results.

## In practice: A practical route

For a workplace goal, read the privacy guide, learn the prompt structure, and choose a task-specific guide. Complete its exercise before exploring automation.

## Try it yourself

Pick one learning outcome for this week and bookmark two relevant lessons.

## Common questions

### Is there a required order?

No. The beginner route is a suggestion. You can choose lessons based on your interests and current knowledge.

### Will completing a path give me a certificate?

This learning center does not issue a certificate. It provides free lessons, exercises, and knowledge checks.

# A quick guide to the quizzes

Learn how question cards, navigation, skipped questions, early submission, and retakes work.

Source: https://lj-web-management.github.io/guides.ai-skills.work/help/take-a-free-ai-quiz/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Publisher: ai-skills.work

## Answer one card at a time

Choose a quiz and start with the first question card. Select one answer, then use Next to continue. Previous lets you revisit earlier cards and change a selection. The progress display shows how many questions you have answered, so you can distinguish navigation from completion.

- There is no timer or account requirement.
- You can leave a question unanswered and return to it.

## Submit when you are ready

You can submit after answering at least one question. If questions remain unanswered, a dialog explains that the results may not be fully accurate. Choose Keep answering to continue or Submit anyway to see a partial result. Submitting a partial quiz is optional.

- An unanswered question is not marked as a wrong answer.
- Partial accuracy is calculated only from answered questions.

## Review and try again

The result shows completion, accuracy on answered questions, and explanations for each item. Use the suggested lesson to review a topic. Retake starts a fresh attempt. Answers are held in the current page session and are not sent to an AI service or saved to an account.

- Reloading the page resets the current attempt.
- Keep results private if you use a shared device.

## In practice: A partial attempt

If you answer four of six questions and get three right, the result shows 4 of 6 answered and 75% accuracy on answered questions. It clearly labels the attempt incomplete.

## Try it yourself

Open a quiz, answer one question, and inspect the early-submission warning before deciding whether to continue.

## Common questions

### Can I submit before finishing?

Yes, after at least one answer. You will see a warning before an incomplete attempt is submitted.

### Are my answers saved?

No account or server-side answer history is created. The current attempt resets when you reload or leave the page.


***

# What your quiz result means

Understand completion, answer accuracy, explanations, and the limits of a short knowledge quiz.

Source: https://lj-web-management.github.io/guides.ai-skills.work/help/understand-quiz-results/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Publisher: ai-skills.work

## Read completion and accuracy together

Completion tells you how much of the quiz you answered. Accuracy tells you how many answered questions were correct. Read both values together. A perfect result from one answered question is much less informative than a completed attempt, and the page labels incomplete attempts clearly.

- Skipped questions are listed separately.
- No overall mastery claim is inferred from a partial attempt.

## Use explanations to find the next lesson

Every question has an explanation of the intended answer. Compare the explanation with your thinking and revisit the relevant guide. A wrong answer is useful feedback about one concept, not a judgment about your ability to learn. Practice applying the idea to a different situation.

- Review correct answers too if you guessed.
- Look for assumptions that affected your choice.

## Understand what the quiz does not measure

These short quizzes sample selected concepts. They do not establish professional competence, grant a credential, or predict job security. Results can be affected by guessing, incomplete answers, familiarity with wording, and the limited number of questions. Use practical exercises and feedback alongside them.

- Do not use the score for hiring or employment decisions.
- Treat improvement as a prompt for further practice.

## In practice: A useful interpretation

You missed a question about checking citations. Read the fact-checking guide and verify three real claims. That practice is more informative than repeatedly selecting the remembered answer.

## Try it yourself

After a quiz, choose one explanation and write a new example that demonstrates the same principle.

## Common questions

### Does a high score make me an AI expert?

No. It indicates performance on a small set of knowledge questions. Expertise requires broader understanding, practice, and appropriate evaluation.

### Does the career quiz predict my job risk?

No. It checks understanding of career-related concepts and does not predict anyone’s employment outcome.

# Need help with ai-skills.work?

Understand the difference between this learning center and the main product, and prepare a useful support question.

Source: https://lj-web-management.github.io/guides.ai-skills.work/help/find-ai-skills-work-help/
Updated: 2026-10-28
Publisher: ai-skills.work

## Find the right place for your question

This learning center contains public lessons and free knowledge quizzes. The main ai-skills.work website is a separate destination. Use the main-site link in the navigation for its current product features and available support channels. Learning center guidance should not be assumed to describe account, billing, or feature behavior on the main product.

- For lesson navigation or quiz behavior, use this help collection.
- For product-specific details, consult the main website’s current information.

## Describe what happened clearly

Record the page, the action you took, what you expected, and what actually happened. Include your browser and device type if relevant. A screenshot can help, but remove personal details, account information, and credentials before sharing it through an appropriate support channel.

- Include an exact error message without sensitive information.
- Mention whether the issue happens consistently.

## Protect your information while troubleshooting

Never share passwords, one-time codes, secret tokens, or payment details in a support description. Use the service’s official secure route when account verification is required. For a learning center issue, refreshing the page resets the current quiz attempt, so finish or note your results first if you want to keep them.

- Confirm that a support link belongs to the intended service.
- Do not grant remote access in response to an unsolicited message.

## In practice: A useful problem report

On the AI basics quiz, using a mobile browser, I selected an answer and tapped Next. I expected the second question but remained on the first card. No error was displayed. This gives a maintainer a concrete behavior to investigate.

## Try it yourself

Write a three-sentence issue description using only fictional details: location, steps, and expected versus actual behavior.

## Common questions

### Are the main site and this learning center the same application?

They are linked destinations. This learning center provides public educational content and quizzes; consult the main site for its product features.

### Where are account and billing instructions?

Use the main website’s verified support information. This guide does not invent account or billing workflows that have not been confirmed.
